To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FTY720 is protective after MCAO for different ischemia durations (3 h and 90 min).
FTY720 is protective in cerebral ischemia and does not increase the rate of bacterial infections in mice.
FTY720 reduces infarct size in a dose dependent manner in two different application models of experimental stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic strategies for acute ischemic stroke, which is the leading cause of adult disability in industrialized countries.
the potential use of FTY720 to treat acute ischemic stroke in humans.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy in the treatment of stroke patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FTY720 does neither promote nor prevent spontaneous infections in experimental stroke.
FTY720 does have a protective effect on ischemic brain tissue and does not seem to be detrimental in terms of spontaneous bacterial infections.
FTY720 is a promising neuroprotective drug with no adverse immunomodulatory effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FTY720 does have a protective effect in stroke but does not promote spontaneous infection.
FTY720 is a promising candidate to reduce the extent of ischemic brain damage and to reduce the rate of spontaneous infections after experimental stroke.
FTY720 does protect against cerebral ischemia without an increased rate of spontaneous infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protective effect of immunomodulatory drugs in experimental stroke is not associated with an increased risk of spontaneous infections.
FTY720 is not associated with an increased rate of spontaneous bacterial infection in experimental stroke.
